metadata.description: A Kubernetes node pool as one orderable deliverable — a Base Class in its own right (ADR-068, ADR-069; promoted out of the former Platform folder). A homogeneous slice of a cluster's node capacity — shared hardware traits, labels, taints — that is ordered, scaled and upgraded on its own (a cloud node pool, a MachineSet, a Cluster API MachineDeployment). The cluster carries no pools of its own: every pool, including the first, is one of these records contained by the cluster, and a cluster with its pools is a composition (ruling 072). Its contract is the Kubernetes node model: every conformant distribution exposes nodes with labels and taints that placement matches workloads against. Named for the standard, never for a product; distribution-specific pool shapes are the Type tier beneath it.

name.description: The node pool name within the cluster (e.g. 'gpu-large', 'general-purpose', 'infra').

cluster_ref.description: Resource reference to a KubernetesCluster (common-elements §2.5, DCM ADR-025). Authored by handle; deferred resolution supported (claim-before-define).

node_count.description: Target number of nodes in this pool.

node_resources.description: Per-node sizing for the pool — the shared compute-sizing shape (common-elements §2.2, ComputeResources) that a VM, a database instance and a node pool all use; size by class (`instance_size`) or by explicit cpu and memory. The provider maps it to a concrete node shape at naturalization (DCM ADR-023). Carried over from the cluster's former inline pool list (ruling 072), which sized nodes as a free-string host shape; the shared shape is comparable across estates and a string is not.

capabilities.description: Queryable capability advertisements — placement policies select pools by capability.

models.description: GPU model names — the observed accelerator model strings (e.g. '<gpu-model>').

labels.description: Labels applied to all nodes in this pool (Kubernetes label semantics).

taints.description: Taints applied to all nodes — workloads must tolerate these to be scheduled on the pool.

relationships.name: cluster
relationships.description: The cluster this node pool belongs to.

context.purpose: Declares a homogeneous slice of a cluster's node capacity — shared hardware traits, labels, taints — that placement matches workloads against.
context.plain_description: A named group of like nodes in a cluster — its `name` is required: how many (`node_count`), what they offer — `capabilities`, where advertisements are structured objects, not booleans (`gpu` carries available/models/count_per_node, beside `architecture` and `memory_tier`) — what `labels` they carry, and what `taints` a workload must tolerate to land there. Placement reads the capability advertisements to match a workload's requirements to a pool. Cloud platforms call this a node pool or machine set.
use_when: You need GPU or otherwise-special nodes grouped so only workloads that need (and tolerate) them land there.
You need placement to select capacity by declared capability (architecture, memory tier) rather than by node names.
not_for: The cluster — KubernetesCluster; it carries no pools of its own (ruling 072).
One physical machine — Machine.BareMetalHost; a pool is a cluster-level grouping, not a host record.
works_with: KubernetesCluster — the cluster the pool belongs to.
KubernetesNamespace — namespaces whose workloads schedule onto pools.
